entries.reader_content_plain:
CHAPTER 24
 
Ge 24:1-9. A Marriage Commission.

1. And Abraham was old ... take a wife--His anxiety to see his son married was natural to his position as a pastoral chief interested in preserving the honor of his tribe, and still more as a patriarch who had regard to the divine promise of a numerous posterity.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv256"/><div sID="gen433" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv256"/><hi type="bold">3. thou shalt not take a wife, &c.--</hi>Among pastoral tribes the matrimonial arrangements are made by the parents, and a youth must marry, not among strangers, but in his own tribe--custom giving him a claim, which is seldom or never resisted, to the hand of his first cousin. But Abraham had a far higher motive--a fear lest, if his son married into a Canaanitish family, he might be gradually led away from the true God. <div eID="gen433" type="x-p"/>
